exercise.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Upright Row
library_steps: Hold a dumbbell in one hand and grip a post with the other.
Pull the dumbbell up close to your body, elbow leading, to chest height.
Lower it slowly. Finish all reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing tall, free hand on a post; the dumbbell starts hanging in front of the thigh, palm toward the body, and is pulled up close to the body, elbow leading and higher than the hand, until the elbow is just under shoulder height and the dumbbell is at lower-chest height.

setup.target: Feet hip-width, knees soft, trunk upright.
Overhand (palm toward the body), dumbbell in front of the thigh, arm long.
setup.why: Upright-row grip; a single dumbbell lets the hand sit out wide like a wide bar grip.

setup.target: Right hand grips an upright post at chest-shoulder height.
Drawn back and steady, not rounded forward.
setup.why: A forward, downward-turned blade narrows the space the upper arm moves through.

movement.measure: elev: upper arm from the side of the trunk, 0 = hanging, 90 = level
movement.start: 25 deg (arm hanging a little forward so the dumbbell clears the thigh)

movement.measure: 0 = out to the side, +90 = straight forward
movement.end: 30 deg (elbow out to the side, a little forward)
about 130 deg (hand below and inside the elbow)

muscles.emg: Concentric activity rose significantly with grip width (p < 0.001), 16 trained men, 85 % 1RM (S1); %MVIC values not in the abstract
muscles.role: Lifts the upper arm out to the side; what the exercise is for (library primary).

muscles.emg: Upper and middle trapezius rose with grip width in the lowering phase (S1); named target in S2
muscles.role: Lifts and turns the shoulder blade upward as the elbow rises.
muscles.surface: Top of the shoulder between neck and acromion.

muscles.emg: Measured, significant change in the lowering phase with grip (S1)
muscles.role: Helps raise the arm, which travels a little in front of the body.
Library secondary; bends the elbow but the load is on the shoulder. Not lit so the shoulder reads as the target; secondary slots are used by trapezius and front delt.

muscles.emg: Concentric activity rose with grip width (S1)

muscles.role: Helps start abduction; under the trapezius.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow above the shoulder / dumbbell to the chin
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Elbow higher than the shoulder at the top.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Raises shoulder impingement risk; S2 stops the elbow at shoulder level, weight at the lower ribs.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Hand higher than the elbow at the top (a curl, not a row).
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a biceps lift; library says elbow leading.

sources.citation: McAllister MJ, Schilling BK, Hammond KG, Weiss LW, Farney TM. 2013. Effect of grip width on electromyographic activity during the upright row. J Strength Cond Res 27(1):181-187.
sources.what_it_gave: 16 trained men, grips 50/100/200 % of shoulder width at 85 % 1RM: wider grip = more deltoid and trapezius, less biceps. Muscles: front, side, rear delt, upper and middle trapezius, biceps.

sources.citation: Hastings B. 2024 (5 Apr). Upright rows. Les Mills.
sources.what_it_gave: Lift only to the lower ribs, elbows no higher than shoulder level, wide grip, shoulder blades back and steady; targets deltoids and traps.
